Ordered an 11-inch Margherita pizza and Chewy Dough Balls and both were extremely poor in quality.

featured_reviews.review_text:
‘Khau’ in Marathi translates to eating, and ‘Galli’ means a lane. There are over 10 Khau Gallis in Mumbai, each is known as the treasure trove of street food in the city. One such street is the Ghatkopar Khau Galli which is popular for its heavenly vegetarian street fare. Recently, we got a chance to prowl this galli and discover a paradise of enticing street food joints, restaurants and stalls. Our bucket list features the best things to try at Ghatkopar Khau Galli.

Directions To Ghatkopar Khau Galli

Ghatkopar Khau Galli is located at a half a kilometre’s distance from Ghatkopar Railway Station (East). Thus, catch a local train or metro to Ghatkopar Railway Station, and then take an auto to Ghatkopar Khau Galli.

Ghatkopar Khau Galli Opening Hours

Business at Ghatkopar Khau Galli commences at around noon and runs until midnight. However, some of the stalls don’t start selling food until 2 pm as preparation takes time.

Variety of dishes with quality of yummy and spicy taste. While loitering around the Ghatkopar Khau Galli, if you come across a restaurant that is preparing 10 dosas at a time, on 10 different tawas, know that you’ve reached Sai Swad Dosa. This eatery is so popular that on weekends you might have to wait for over 40 minutes to get your order. The remarkable factor about this dosa joint is that they do not ever compromise on the hygiene and quality of the dishes. The cooks here always use requisite equipment and only the freshest ingredients. They serve 45 different varieties of dosa, the most popular one being the Gini Dosa, which is slathered with Szechuan sauce and is dripping with melting cheese.

What to have: Gini Dosa, Pasta Dosa, Maggi Dosa, Cheese Chocolate Dosa

Perfect for: Evening Snacks

This place has a comfortable aura and interiors of this casual dining restaurant are appealing.
The cuisine is focused on traditional Indian featuring the regions of Awadh, Rajasthan and North West Frontier India. These flavours are influenced by local culture bringing out the authenticity to provide a world class gastronomic experience. The food is absolutely amazing – everything we tasted melted in other mouths especially GALAWAT KE KEBAB and LUCKNAWI GOSHT DUM BIRYANI. Absolutely the best meal we had
At Nawab Saheb you can enjoy culturally rich traditional dining experience which stays in your memory.

featured_reviews.name: Mahek Khanna
featured_reviews.review_text:
Renaissance Hotel Powai is nothing short of royal and beautiful. Simply amazing hospitality and such pretty restaurants. This Infact, was my reason to visit Nawab Saheb for their ongoing Tawa & Tandoor Festival (20th- 28th September) as there are very few restaurants who actually go out of their way to curate special menus like these. Brainchild of Chef Yunus Khan, I think everything on the menu was fantastic. Service was slow as the restaurant was quite packed, being a Friday night. I opted for the vegetarian fare priced at 2800. Frankly, I thought it was value for money only because of the main course. Just their dal makhani and paneer will leave you licking your fingers till the end. Here's what the spread consisted of and how I felt about it :
Vegetarian :
1. Til Malai ka Phool (5/5)- Melt in the mouth brocolli with cream cheese. Found the cauliflower okayish.
2. Chef Yunus Khan ka Paneer Tikka (10/5)- Star dish! Has to be the best I've had in a long time. Highly recommended.
3. Subz ki Ashraphiya (3/5)- Found it average.
4. Bhune Bhutte ke Seekh (5/5)- AMAZING combination of seekh Kebab and babycorn. YUM.
5. Kabuki Kebab (3/5)- Found it too dry. Taste wise as well, bland due to Chickpeas.
6. Chukunder ke Kebab (4/5)- Beetroot galauti, it was nice.
7. Kumbh ke Galawat (5/5)- Wow. Has to be the one thing I'd come back for! Surprisingly it was served on a thepla kind of bread.
8. Aloo Atishi (4/5)- Bharwan aloo, classic.

Mains :
1. Paneer Kaliyan (10/5)- Now that's what I'm talking about. It's dishes like these that make you remember these hotels. No one does mains like them. I ALWAYS skip mains but yesterday I was too tempted after a bite and ended up having 3 pieces of bread after such heavy array of starters. MY FAVOURITE FROM YESTERDAY because it was cashew gravy, so creamy, soft paneer chunks and rightly spiced. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.
2. Daal Nawab (10/5)- Probably as good as the one I've had in Delhi at ITC. Properly slow cooked for 48 hours, perfectly creamy and texture was just right. Not overdone. Yum.
3. Subz Biryani - couldn't dare to try it. Was too full.

Desserts : Assorted variety
Motichoor Laddoo, Kaju Katli, Kalakand, Gulab Jamun, Akhroti Halwa, Phirni - all were great but my favourites were the Phirni and Gulab Jamun.

Great staff and great hospitality by team. Special thanks to Manager Avanish, steward Shrikant and Chef Rahul Karve.

This place has maintained not just the standards but also taste of the food. The staff was very welcoming and warm with hospitality. Nawab Saheb is a gastronomical journey for those exploring the ageless Royal Mughlai and North Indian Cuisine.
